selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Seoul, South Korea

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the grand Joseon-era Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok rental. Wearing Hanbok grants free palace entry. Witness the ceremonial guard changing and wander through the National Folk Museum within the palace grounds for a deep dive into Korean royal history and culture.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into one of Seoul's oldest and most iconic traditional markets. Sample authentic Korean street food including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). This is a true local culinary institution beloved by Seoulites and food lovers worldwide.

experiences.name: K-Pop & Hallyu Culture Tour in Hongdae
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Seoul's vibrant K-culture hub. Visit K-pop entertainment agency storefronts, browse idol merchandise shops, catch live busking performances by aspiring artists, explore K-pop themed cafes, and visit the SM, YG, or HYBE flagship stores. End the evening at a norebang (private karaoke room) for the ultimate K-culture experience.

experiences.name: Korean Temple Stay at Jogyesa Temple
experiences.description: Participate in a half-day temple life program at Jogyesa, the head temple of Korean Buddhism located in central Seoul. Experience meditation, tea ceremony, monk-led dharma talks, and the art of making prayer beads (108 bead bracelet). Gain rare insight into Korean Buddhist traditions and find tranquility in the heart of the bustling city.

experiences.name: Korean Cooking Class & Banchan Workshop
experiences.description: Join a hands-on Korean cooking class where you learn to prepare iconic dishes such as kimchi jjigae, japchae, and a variety of banchan (side dishes). Led by a local chef, the class includes a market visit to source fresh ingredients, step-by-step cooking instruction, and a communal meal to enjoy your creations. A perfect blend of food, culture, and local interaction.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Seoul, South Korea

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives late evening
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Take the AREX (Airport Railroad Express) to Seoul Station or a limousine bus to your accommodation area. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in. Grab a quick late-night snack from a nearby convenience store (GS25 or CU) — try triangle kimbap, instant ramen, or hotteok.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Convenience store late-night snack: triangle kimbap + cup ramen (under ₩5,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: AREX train from Incheon to Seoul Station costs about ₩9,500. T-money card is highly recommended — purchase one at the airport convenience store for ₩4,000 and load it with ₩30,000–₩50,000 for easy subway and bus travel. December in Seoul is cold (around -2°C to 5°C), so layer up immediately.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. Have a slow morning at the hotel. Walk around the immediate neighborhood to orient yourself. Visit a local bakery chain like Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours for a cheap breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁) — the most iconic royal palace in Seoul. Entry is only ₩3,000. Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) near the palace gates for ₩15,000–₩20,000/hour and get free entry while wearing it. Explore the palace grounds and visit the National Folk Museum of Korea inside (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Bukchon Hanok Village (북촌한옥마을) — a beautifully preserved traditional Korean village with narrow alleys and historic hanok houses. Completely free to walk around. Then head to Insadong (인사동) for dinner and evening browsing of traditional craft shops, street food stalls, and tea houses.

meals.breakfast: Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours — coffee + pastry (₩4,000–₩6,000)
meals.lunch: Bibimbap or doenjang jjigae at a local restaurant near Gyeongbokgung (₩7,000–₩9,000)
meals.dinner: Insadong street food — hotteok (sweet pancake), tteokbokki, and odeng (fish cake skewers) (₩5,000–₩8,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays but open Wednesday. Wear warm layers — palace grounds are very exposed in December wind. Bukchon is best visited in the afternoon for good light photos. Be respectful of residents still living in the village.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁) and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). Entry is ₩3,000 for the palace; Secret Garden guided tour is ₩5,000 extra. Book the English-language Secret Garden tour in advance online. This UNESCO World Heritage Site is stunning even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Changgyeonggung Palace (창경궁) — entry ₩1,000 — and then head to Jongmyo Shrine (종묘), a UNESCO-listed royal ancestral shrine (₩1,000 entry). These three sites form a connected royal heritage trail in the heart of Seoul.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Dongdaemun (동대문) area for the evening. Visit Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a futuristic landmark by Zaha Hadid — free to walk around outside. Browse the massive Dongdaemun Market for budget shopping and street food. Try a bowl of seolleongtang (ox bone soup) at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area convenience store or street vendor — egg toast (계란 토스트) ₩2,000–₩3,000
meals.lunch: Gimbap Cheonguk or local kimbap restaurant near Changdeokgung — kimbap + ramen combo (₩5,000–₩7,000)
meals.dinner: Seolleongtang (ox bone soup) at a local Dongdaemun restaurant (₩9,000–₩12,000)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Secret Garden English tour at the official palace website (heritage.go.kr) at least a day in advance as spots are limited. DDP often has free outdoor exhibitions and light installations, especially in winter — worth checking their schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Hongdae (홍대) — Seoul's youth culture and K-indie music hub. Explore the vibrant street art, murals, and quirky cafés. Visit the free street performances area and browse unique vintage and indie shops along the main streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Sinchon (신촌) and Ewha Womans University area — the university campus itself is architecturally beautiful and free to enter. Browse the student shopping streets for affordable Korean fashion and accessories. Visit a themed café (animal café, dessert café, etc.) — a very K-culture experience (₩8,000–₩12,000 including a drink).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Han River (한강) — take the subway to Yeouido or Mangwon station. Buy convenience store fried chicken and beer (chimaek!) and enjoy it on the riverside park benches like locals do. Watch the city lights reflect on the river at night. Dress very warmly — it will be cold by the river.

meals.breakfast: Hongdae area café — Americano + egg sandwich (₩5,000–₩7,000)
meals.lunch: Sinchon area — sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a local restaurant (₩7,000–₩9,000)
meals.dinner: Han River convenience store chimaek (fried chicken + beer/soda) — GS25 or CU riverside branch (₩12,000–₩15,000)

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is extremely lively on Friday evenings with buskers and street performers — consider coming back here in the evening another day. Han River parks have heated rest areas in winter. Yeouido Hangang Park has better facilities; Mangwon is more local and less touristy.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namdaemun Market (남대문시장) — one of Seoul's oldest and largest traditional markets. Open very early. Explore stalls selling everything from street food to clothing, kitchenware, and souvenirs. Try the famous Namdaemun kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk uphill to Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower) — you can hike up Namsan Mountain for free (about 40 minutes) or take the cable car (₩12,000 round trip). The tower observation deck costs ₩21,000 but the outdoor deck and love lock area are free. Enjoy panoramic 360° views of Seoul. On a clear winter day, visibility is excellent.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Myeongdong (명동) — Seoul's most famous shopping and street food district. Sample Korean street food: tteokbokki, corn dogs, steamed dumplings (mandu), tornado potatoes, and more. Browse K-beauty stores like Innisfree, Etude House, and The Face Shop for affordable skincare products (great souvenirs).

meals.breakfast: Namdaemun Market — kalguksu or hotteok (₩4,000–₩7,000)
meals.lunch: Namsan area packed lunch from convenience store or bring snacks from Namdaemun (₩5,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food crawl — tteokbokki, mandu, corn dog, and fish cake (₩8,000–₩12,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means Namdaemun and Myeongdong will be very crowded — go to Namdaemun early (before 10am) for a calmer experience. The hike up Namsan is free and very popular with locals; paths are lit at night. Myeongdong vendors are open late (until 10–11pm).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located in central Seoul. Entry is free. The temple is beautifully decorated in winter. Attend a morning ceremony if you wake up early enough (starts around 4am or 10am). Nearby Templestay programs are available for a deeper cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gwanghwamun Square (광화문광장) to see the statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin. Visit the underground King Sejong Museum (₩3,000) for Korean history and the invention of Hangul. Walk along Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) — a beautiful restored urban stream perfect for a winter stroll (free).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Ikseon-dong Hanok Village (익선동) — a trendy, Instagram-worthy neighborhood with traditional hanok buildings converted into hip cafés, cocktail bars, and fusion restaurants. Very photogenic at night with warm lighting. Have dinner at one of the fusion Korean restaurants here.

meals.breakfast: Temple area — kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) at a local restaurant (₩6,000–₩8,000)
meals.lunch: Cheonggyecheon area — dosirak (Korean lunch box) from a local restaurant or food court (₩7,000–₩9,000)
meals.dinner: Ikseon-dong — fusion Korean cuisine at a hanok restaurant (₩12,000–₩15,000)

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple hosts lantern festivals and special events in winter — check their schedule. Cheonggyecheon Stream is heated in sections during winter. Ikseon-dong gets very busy on Sunday evenings — arrive before 6pm for shorter waits at popular spots.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원화성) — take the subway from Seoul to Suwon Station (about 1 hour, ₩1,400 on T-money). The fortress is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with massive stone walls you can walk along. Entry is ₩1,000. Enjoy winter views of the fortress and surrounding city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's traditional market area near the fortress. Visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace (행궁) — the temporary palace within the fortress grounds (₩1,500 entry). Watch traditional Korean archery demonstrations if available. Head back to Seoul by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul and explore the Itaewon (이태원) area — Seoul's most international neighborhood with diverse food options, multicultural shops, and a vibrant nightlife scene. Visit Gyeongnidan-gil (경리단길) — a charming street with indie restaurants and cafés just uphill from Itaewon station.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or convenience store before departure (₩3,000–₩5,000)
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (수원갈비) — Suwon is famous for its grilled short ribs; find a budget set at a local restaurant (₩12,000–₩15,000)
meals.dinner: Itaewon/Gyeongnidan-gil — international cuisine (Thai, Indian, Mexican) at budget prices (₩10,000–₩14,000)

day_by_day.notes: The Suwon Hwaseong fortress walls offer a great winter walk with fewer tourists than summer. Bring hand warmers as the fortress walls are very exposed to wind. The round trip subway fare from Seoul to Suwon is approximately ₩2,800 total.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) in Yongsan — one of the most comprehensive war museums in Asia. Entry is FREE. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the extensive exhibits covering Korean history from ancient battles to the Korean War. Outdoor exhibits include tanks, aircraft, and warships.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Yongsan Electronics Market (용산전자상가) — a massive complex of electronics shops, great for browsing the latest Korean tech gadgets, K-pop merchandise, and accessories. Then visit Hangang Bridge area for a winter riverside walk. Take the subway to Noryangjin Fish Market (노량진수산시장) to see one of Seoul's largest wholesale fish markets.
day_by_day.evening: At Noryangjin Fish Market, pick fresh seafood from the market stalls and have it cooked at one of the upstairs restaurants for a small cooking fee. This is an authentic and surprisingly affordable Korean seafood experience. Try raw fish (hoe), grilled shellfish, or spicy seafood stew.

meals.breakfast: Yongsan area — haejang-guk (hangover soup/hearty morning soup) at a local restaurant (₩7,000–₩9,000)
meals.lunch: War Memorial café or nearby convenience store (₩5,000–₩7,000)
meals.dinner: Noryangjin Fish Market — pick your seafood + cooking fee (₩15,000–₩25,000 depending on selection)

day_by_day.notes: The War Memorial is closed on Mondays but open on Tuesdays. Noryangjin Fish Market is open 24 hours — the evening is a great time to visit as the market is active and atmospheric. Bring cash as some vendors prefer it.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World (롯데월드) in Jamsil — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks. Budget option: purchase just the Magic Pass for selected rides (₩30,000–₩35,000) instead of the full day pass (₩62,000). Alternatively, visit the adjacent Lotte World Folk Museum (₩5,000) for Korean cultural history without the theme park cost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Seokchon Lake (석촌호수) next to Lotte World — a beautiful free lake park. In December, there may be winter light installations around the lake. Visit Lotte World Tower Sky31 Observatory (₩27,000) for incredible city views, or admire the tower's exterior for free from the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the COEX Mall (코엑스몰) in Gangnam — Asia's largest underground shopping mall. Visit the stunning COEX Library (별마당 도서관) — a free public library with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, a Seoul landmark. Browse the mall and have dinner at the food court.

meals.breakfast: Jamsil area — gyeran bap (egg rice) or a local breakfast set (₩5,000–₩7,000)
meals.lunch: Lotte World food court or nearby — tteokbokki + sundae (Korean blood sausage) combo (₩7,000–₩9,000)
meals.dinner: COEX Mall food court — Korean BBQ set or bibimbap (₩9,000–₩12,000)

day_by_day.notes: If budget is very tight, skip Lotte World theme park entirely and just enjoy the free lake and mall areas. The COEX Library is free and absolutely worth visiting — it's one of Seoul's most photogenic modern spaces. December 23rd may have Christmas decorations throughout COEX.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gangnam (강남) area — walk along the famous Gangnam-daero boulevard. See the Gangnam Style statue near KEPCO Plaza (free photo op). Visit the underground Gangnam underground shopping arcade for cheap Korean fashion and accessories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Apgujeong Rodeo Street (압구정 로데오) and Garosu-gil (가로수길) — tree-lined streets with boutiques, cafés, and K-pop agency buildings. This is the heart of Seoul's luxury and K-culture scene. Visit SM Entertainment's SM Town COEX Artium (free entry to building; some exhibits may have fees) for K-pop fan culture.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul! Head to Myeongdong Cathedral (명동성당) for the Christmas Eve mass — a beautiful Gothic cathedral in the heart of Seoul, open to all visitors. The area will be decorated with lights and festive stalls. Join locals celebrating Christmas in one of Seoul's most atmospheric evenings of the year.

meals.breakfast: Gangnam area bakery — croissant + latte (₩5,000–₩7,000)
meals.lunch: Garosu-gil café with a light Korean meal set (₩10,000–₩13,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong area — Christmas Eve street food and festive stalls, or a sit-down Korean restaurant (₩10,000–₩15,000)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is very festive in Seoul — Koreans celebrate it as a couple's holiday similar to Valentine's Day. Myeongdong will be crowded but magical with lights. Book dinner reservations in advance if you want a sit-down restaurant as many places will be full. The cathedral mass is a memorable cultural experience even for non-Christians.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park (북한산국립공원) — a stunning mountain park right within Seoul city limits. Take the subway to Ui Station and hike the Bukhansanseong Fortress Trail (moderate difficulty, about 2–3 hours round trip). Incredible winter mountain scenery with snow-dusted peaks. Entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Korea (국립중앙박물관) in Yongsan — one of the largest museums in the world with 12,000+ artifacts. Entry is FREE. Spend 2–3 hours exploring Korean history from prehistoric times to the Joseon Dynasty. The museum grounds are also beautiful for a winter walk.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Itaewon for Christmas dinner — the neighborhood has many international restaurants celebrating Christmas with special menus. Alternatively, head to a Korean BBQ restaurant for a festive self-grilled dinner — a uniquely Korean Christmas experience.

meals.breakfast: Pack a convenience store snack for the hike — kimbap rolls + energy drink (₩4,000–₩6,000)
meals.lunch: Post-hike — doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean paste stew) at a local restaurant near the park (₩7,000–₩9,000)
meals.dinner: Korean BBQ (삼겹살 - grilled pork belly) at a local KBBQ restaurant — Christmas treat! (₩15,000–₩20,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan can be icy in December — bring hiking poles if possible and wear proper grip shoes. The National Museum is closed on Mondays but open on Christmas Day (Friday). Many restaurants may have limited menus on Christmas Day — check in advance or have a backup convenience store option.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hongdae again for a deeper exploration — this time visit the Free Market (프리마켓) at Hongdae if it's running on weekends (check schedule). Browse indie artist stalls, handmade crafts, and K-indie music performances. Visit the KT&G Sangsang Madang cultural complex for free art exhibitions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Digital Media City (DMC) area and visit the Haneul Park (하늘공원) — a hilltop park with panoramic city views, part of the World Cup Park complex. In winter, the silver grass (억새) creates a beautiful misty landscape. Free entry. Then visit the nearby Mapo Oil Tank Culture Park (문화비축기지) — a unique cultural space in repurposed oil tanks (free).
day_by_day.evening: Final major shopping evening at Namdaemun Market and Myeongdong for last-minute souvenirs and K-beauty products. Stock up on Korean snacks, dried seaweed, instant ramen, and cosmetics as gifts. Have a farewell Korean dinner at a traditional restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hongdae area — Korean egg toast from a street cart (₩2,500–₩3,500)
meals.lunch: Mapo area — sundubu jjigae or kimchi jjigae at a local restaurant (₩7,000–₩9,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong — galbi-tang (short rib soup) or samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) at a traditional restaurant (₩12,000–₩16,000)

day_by_day.notes: Haneul Park requires a short uphill walk (about 10–15 minutes from the parking lot). The views of the Han River and Seoul skyline from the top are spectacular, especially at sunset. Namdaemun Market vendors will be busy on Saturday — arrive before 5pm for the best selection before evening crowds peak.

day_by_day.morning: Last morning in Seoul — wake up early and visit a local jjimjilbang (찜질방 - Korean bathhouse/sauna) for a final Korean cultural experience. Many are open 24 hours. Entry is typically ₩10,000–₩15,000 and includes access to hot baths, saunas, and rest areas. A quintessential Korean experience to end the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack up and check out of the hotel. Store luggage at the hotel or at a nearby coin locker (subway stations have them for ₩2,000–₩4,000/day). Take a final stroll through your neighborhood. Visit any last spots you missed or want to revisit. Head to the airport with plenty of time — take the AREX from Seoul Station (about 43 minutes to Incheon, ₩9,500).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Incheon International Airport. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before your flight for international departures. Browse duty-free shops for any last Korean products (Korean cosmetics and snacks are popular duty-free items).

meals.breakfast: Jjimjilbang — sikhye (sweet rice drink) + hard-boiled eggs, the traditional jjimjilbang snack (₩2,000–₩3,000)
meals.lunch: Airport or neighborhood — bibimbap or a comforting Korean meal before departure (₩9,000–₩12,000)
meals.dinner: Airport food court or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is usually noon — confirm with your hotel. The AREX train to Incheon Airport runs from Seoul Station and City Air Terminal. You can check in your luggage at Seoul Station (City Check-in service) up to 3 hours before your flight, which saves you carrying bags on the train. Keep some Korean won for last-minute expenses but exchange or spend remaining won before departure as it's difficult to exchange outside Korea.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Seoul, South Korea

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, then take the AREX Express Train or airport limousine bus to your hotel in Seoul. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your room.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24-hour convenience store (GS25 or CU) near the hotel — try triangle kimbap, instant ramen, or hotteok for an authentic Korean late-night experience

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you've had a long flight. Hydrate well and get a good night's rest. Exchange some currency at the airport (Wonbucks) or withdraw KRW from an ATM. Pick up a T-money transit card at the airport convenience store for easy subway and bus travel throughout your trip.

day_by_day.morning: Start your Seoul adventure with a visit to Gyeongbokgung Palace, the grandest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Arrive early (opens 9:00 AM) to watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 AM. Consider renting a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) from a nearby rental shop — hanbok wearers get free palace entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village, a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Stroll the winding alleys, admire the architecture, and stop at small artisan shops and galleries. Continue to Insadong Street for browsing K-culture souvenirs, tea houses, and traditional crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gwangjang Market, one of Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional markets. Explore the vibrant food stalls and soak in the lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café — try a Korean-style breakfast of doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) and rice at a local restaurant
meals.lunch: Eat at a small restaurant near Insadong — try bibimbap (mixed rice bowl) or sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) for around 8,000–12,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market: bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), or yukhoe (Korean beef tartare) — budget around 10,000–15,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung Palace is closed on Tuesdays. Since today is Wednesday, it will be open. Dress warmly — December in Seoul is cold (average 0–5°C). The Royal Guard Ceremony runs at 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). Book the Secret Garden guided tour in advance as spots are limited. The garden is stunning even in winter with bare trees and traditional pavilions dusted with possible snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Jongno district and visit Jogyesa Temple, the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated with lanterns during winter. Then head to Cheonggyecheon Stream for a peaceful walk along this restored urban waterway.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the vibrant Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a futuristic architectural landmark by Zaha Hadid. Explore the shopping complex and night market stalls surrounding it.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel or hotel breakfast — try a patbingsu café for a warm Korean bun or hotteok
meals.lunch: Try Korean set lunch (백반, baekban) near Jongno — a full spread of rice, soup, and multiple side dishes for around 8,000–10,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area: try dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) or tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes) at a local pojangmacha (street food tent) — around 10,000–15,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Book the Changdeokgung Secret Garden tour online at the official palace website in advance. Tours run several times daily and last about 90 minutes. Bring a portable hand warmer for the outdoor garden tour.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Myeongdong, Seoul's most famous shopping and beauty district. Browse K-beauty shops (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), street food stalls, and international brands. This is prime territory for K-culture shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up to Namsan Mountain and visit N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower). Take the cable car up for panoramic views of the city. Attach a love lock to the famous fence and enjoy the observation deck views — spectacular on a clear winter day.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Myeongdong for the evening street food market, which comes alive at night. Then explore the nearby명동 area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast or a bakery chain like Paris Baguette or Tous les Jours near the hotel
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food: egg bread (계란빵), corn dogs, grilled skewers, and hotteok — budget around 5,000–10,000 KRW for a filling street food lunch
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja restaurant (famous for kalguksu hand-cut noodle soup and mandu dumplings) — around 10,000–14,000 KRW per person

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower observation deck admission is around 21,000 KRW for adults. The cable car costs about 9,000 KRW round trip. Alternatively, you can hike up Namsan for free (about 30–40 minutes). Myeongdong is very crowded on weekends, so enjoy it today on a Friday before the weekend rush.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Hongdae (Hongik University area), the heart of Seoul's youth culture, indie music, and K-pop scene. Explore the street art, quirky shops, and café culture. Visit the Hongdae Free Market area and browse the creative stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Sinchon district and then walk to the Han River (Hangang) at Yeouido. Rent a bicycle (available year-round) or simply stroll along the riverside park. In winter, enjoy the crisp air and the peaceful riverside scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the vibrant nightlife scene. Catch a live busking performance (common on weekends), explore the themed cafés, and experience the K-pop culture clubs or noraebangs (private karaoke rooms).

meals.breakfast: Brunch at a trendy Hongdae café — try Korean brunch sets or avocado toast with Korean fusion twists, around 12,000–18,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Try jjajangmyeon (black bean noodles) or jjamppong (spicy seafood noodle soup) at a Chinese-Korean restaurant in Hongdae — around 8,000–12,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) at a local BBQ restaurant in Hongdae — around 15,000–20,000 KRW per person including side dishes and drinks

day_by_day.notes: Norebang (karaoke) is a quintessential K-culture experience — rooms typically cost 15,000–25,000 KRW per hour for a private room. Hongdae is busiest on Saturday nights, making it the perfect night to experience Seoul's youth culture at its peak.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (about 1 hour by subway from Seoul). This UNESCO World Heritage fortress walls stretch 5.7 km and offer beautiful winter walks with historical significance. Visit the Hwaseong Haenggung Palace inside the fortress.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the fortress walls — walk the full circuit or take the Hwaseong Tour Train. Visit the Suwon Traditional Market (Paldalmun Market) nearby for local street food and produce.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul and relax in the Itaewon neighborhood — Seoul's most international district with diverse restaurants, bars, and shops. Great for a casual Sunday evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab something at Seoul Station before taking the subway to Suwon
meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (Suwon-style short ribs) — a local specialty of Suwon, around 15,000–25,000 KRW per person at a restaurant near the fortress
meals.dinner: Itaewon: try a Korean-fusion restaurant or explore the diverse international food scene — Thai, Mexican, Indian options all available around 15,000–25,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Take subway Line 1 from Seoul Station to Suwon Station (about 55 minutes, 2,500 KRW). From Suwon Station, take a local bus or taxi to the fortress (about 10 minutes). The fortress is open daily and admission is 1,000 KRW for adults.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums with an incredible collection of Korean artifacts, art, and history spanning thousands of years. Admission is free for the permanent collection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the War Memorial of Korea nearby — a powerful and moving museum dedicated to Korean military history, including the Korean War. The outdoor exhibition of military equipment is impressive. Free admission.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the trendy Gangnam district (made famous by PSY's Gangnam Style). Explore the upscale COEX Mall — one of Asia's largest underground shopping complexes — and visit the stunning Starfield Library inside COEX.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café
meals.lunch: Museum café at the National Museum of Korea or grab bibimbap at a nearby restaurant — around 10,000–13,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Gangnam area: try a modern Korean restaurant or visit the COEX food court for a variety of Korean dishes — around 12,000–20,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays — adjust by visiting the War Memorial first (open Monday) and then spending more time at COEX and Gangnam in the afternoon. The Starfield Library inside COEX is a must-see Instagram-worthy spot.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea (rescheduled from Day 7 — now open on Tuesday). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the permanent galleries covering prehistoric Korea through the Joseon Dynasty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Lotte World in Jamsil — a massive indoor/outdoor theme park and entertainment complex. Even if you're not into rides, the area around Lotte World Tower (the 5th tallest building in the world) is spectacular. Visit the Seoul Sky observation deck on the 117th–123rd floors for breathtaking views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Seokchon Lake Park surrounding Lotte World — beautifully lit with winter illuminations. The area around Jamsil is great for evening dining and shopping.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local Korean breakfast restaurant — try haejang-guk (hangover soup) or congee
meals.lunch: Lotte World food court or nearby restaurant — try Korean fried chicken (치킨, chikin) which is a Korean staple, around 15,000–20,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Jamsil area: try a traditional Korean BBQ restaurant for galbi (beef short ribs) — around 20,000–30,000 KRW per person

day_by_day.notes: Seoul Sky observation deck admission is approximately 29,000 KRW for adults. Book online in advance to avoid queues. Lotte World Theme Park day passes are around 62,000 KRW if you want to experience the rides. December often features special winter light shows at Lotte World.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the hip and trendy Seongsu-dong neighborhood — often called the 'Brooklyn of Seoul.' Browse independent boutiques, artisan coffee shops set in converted warehouses, and unique concept stores. This area is a favorite for Korean millennials and creatives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Seoul Forest (서울숲) nearby — a large urban park perfect for a winter stroll. Then head to the Ttukseom area along the Han River for riverside views. Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art in Hannam for world-class contemporary and traditional Korean art.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hannam-dong for dinner — one of Seoul's most upscale and trendy neighborhoods with excellent restaurants, wine bars, and boutique shops.

meals.breakfast: Specialty coffee and brunch at one of Seongsu-dong's famous café-roasteries — a must for coffee lovers, around 8,000–15,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Seongsu-dong: try a trendy Korean fusion restaurant or a popular local spot — around 12,000–18,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Hannam-dong: try makgeolli (traditional Korean rice wine) pairing at a traditional Korean restaurant, or enjoy modern Korean cuisine — around 20,000–30,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Seongsu-dong is best explored on foot. The area has transformed rapidly and is filled with pop-up stores and concept cafés that change seasonally. Leeum Museum of Art admission is approximately 10,000 KRW. Check their website for current exhibitions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple in the morning for a peaceful cultural experience. Then explore the nearby Insa-dong area once more for last-minute souvenir shopping and to browse the traditional tea houses — a calm way to start Christmas Eve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Cheongdam-dong and Apgujeong — Seoul's luxury fashion district and K-pop heartland. Visit SM Town (SM Entertainment's flagship store and museum), YG Republic, or the HYBE Insight museum (home of BTS) — essential for K-culture fans. Book HYBE Insight tickets in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Christmas Eve in Seoul — Koreans celebrate Christmas as a couple's holiday and the city is beautifully decorated. Head to Myeongdong Cathedral (명동성당) for Christmas Eve services or simply admire the decorations. Then explore the festive Cheonggyecheon Stream light festival.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast at a tea house in Insadong — try omija tea and tteok (rice cakes)
meals.lunch: Apgujeong area: try a trendy Korean café lunch or visit a popular local restaurant — around 15,000–20,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special dinner — treat yourself to a slightly elevated Korean dining experience. Try a Korean course meal (한정식, hanjeongsik) — around 30,000–50,000 KRW per person for a special occasion

day_by_day.notes: HYBE Insight museum requires advance booking and sells out quickly — book as early as possible. The museum offers immersive experiences related to BTS and other HYBE artists. Christmas Eve in Seoul is magical with city-wide decorations and a festive atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea. Start with a relaxed morning — visit one of Seoul's beautiful palaces (Deoksugung Palace is particularly atmospheric in winter) for a peaceful Christmas morning stroll. The Stone Wall Road (Deoksugung Doldam-gil) alongside the palace is one of Seoul's most romantic walks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Seoul Museum of History near Gyeongbokgung for a deep dive into Seoul's urban history — free admission. Then explore the nearby Gyeonghuigung Palace (less touristy, more serene). Spend the afternoon at a traditional Korean tea ceremony experience in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Bukchon or Samcheong-dong for a magical Christmas evening walk through the illuminated hanok village streets. Enjoy the festive atmosphere unique to Seoul's blend of Korean tradition and Christmas celebration.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — relax and enjoy a leisurely Christmas morning meal
meals.lunch: Try Korean Christmas food — many Koreans eat fried chicken and pizza on Christmas. Enjoy Korean fried chicken (BBQ or Kyochon) — around 20,000–25,000 KRW for a whole chicken
meals.dinner: Samcheong-dong: cozy Korean restaurant dinner — try doenjang jjigae, japchae (glass noodles), and assorted banchan side dishes in a warm, traditional setting — around 15,000–25,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Many attractions and restaurants are open on Christmas Day in Seoul. Korean Christmas is celebrated differently from Western traditions — it's more of a romantic couple's day and commercial holiday. Enjoy the unique cultural blend of Korean and Western Christmas traditions.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Nami Island (남이섬) — a beautiful river island about 1.5 hours from Seoul by bus/train and ferry. Famous for its tree-lined avenues and natural beauty, it's magical in winter with bare trees and possible snow. It gained international fame from the K-drama 'Winter Sonata.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nami Island — rent a bicycle, visit the ostriches and other animals on the island, and enjoy the serene winter landscape. Optionally combine with a stop at Petite France or the Garden of Morning Calm nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul and head to the lively Sinchon or Edae (Ewha Womans University) area for evening shopping and dining — popular with Korean university students and great for affordable K-fashion.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or grab something at the bus terminal before departure
meals.lunch: Nami Island has several restaurants — try Korean set meals or ramyeon on the island, around 10,000–15,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Sinchon/Edae area: try Korean army stew (부대찌개, budae jjigae) — a hearty, flavorful stew with sausage, ramen, and vegetables — around 12,000–15,000 KRW per person

day_by_day.notes: Take the ITX-Cheongchun train from Yongsan Station to Gapyeong Station (about 70 minutes, 5,200 KRW), then a local taxi or shuttle to the Nami Island ferry dock. Ferry costs about 3,000 KRW round trip. Nami Island admission is 16,000 KRW for adults. Book the train in advance on Korail website.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — revisit your favorite neighborhood or explore any spots you missed. Consider a final visit to a traditional market like Namdaemun Market (the largest traditional market in Korea) for last-minute souvenir shopping and street food.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack and prepare for departure. Do a final walk around your hotel neighborhood to soak in the last moments of Seoul. Visit a nearby jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/bathhouse) for a relaxing pre-departure experience — a quintessentially Korean way to end your trip.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport via AREX Express Train from Seoul Station (about 43 minutes to Incheon Airport, 9,500 KRW) or airport limousine bus. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before your flight for international departure. Enjoy your last Korean meal at the airport.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — final Korean hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market: enjoy a final Korean street food feast — hotteok, kalguksu, bindaetteok — around 5,000–10,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport has excellent restaurants on the departure level — enjoy a final bowl of Korean ramen, bibimbap, or samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) before your flight — around 12,000–18,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Return your T-money card at the airport for a refund of the remaining balance (minus a 500 KRW service fee). Duty-free shopping is available throughout Incheon Airport. Keep some KRW cash for final purchases or convert remaining currency back at the airport exchange. Incheon Airport is consistently rated one of the world's best airports — arrive early and enjoy the facilities!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Seoul, South Korea

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury airport transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort, Seoul. Check-in, unwind, and settle into your premium beachfront suite. Enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the resort.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining or resort lounge — light Korean-inspired supper such as Japchae, Doenjang Jjigae, and premium Korean teas

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 light — rest is essential after a long-haul flight. Confirm check-in details with resort prior to arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late start. Enjoy a lavish breakfast at the resort. Take a gentle orientation walk around the resort grounds and nearby coastal area to acclimate. Visit a nearby traditional Korean tea house for a morning tea ceremony introduction.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of Gyeongbokgung Palace — the grandest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Witness the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony. Explore the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace grounds for an immersive introduction to Korean history and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Bukchon Hanok Village as the evening lights illuminate the traditional hanok rooftops. Enjoy a private sunset photo session with a professional photographer dressed in rented Hanbok attire.

meals.breakfast: Resort's signature breakfast buffet featuring both Western and Korean options including Kongnamul Gukbap and premium pastries
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang — a legendary restaurant near Gyeongbokgung famed for its premium Ginseng Chicken Soup
meals.dinner: Jungsik Seoul — a Michelin two-starred modern Korean restaurant offering an exquisite tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungsik Seoul well in advance. Hanbok rental near Gyeongbokgung Palace is available from several premium studios. Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays.

day_by_day.morning: Private morning visit to Changdeokgung Palace and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon). A knowledgeable private guide will narrate the Joseon Dynasty history. The winter garden offers a serene, frost-kissed beauty unique to December.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Insadong — Seoul's premier cultural and antique district. Browse high-end galleries, traditional craft shops, and Korean paper (hanji) art studios. Visit Ssamziegil, a unique courtyard complex with artisan boutiques and cultural installations.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a private K-culture performance evening — a curated show featuring traditional Korean music (Gugak), fan dance (Buchaechum), and mask dance (Talchum) at a premium cultural venue.

meals.breakfast: In-resort Korean breakfast: Doenjang Jjigae, steamed rice, assorted banchan, and fresh seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Balwoo Gongyang — a celebrated temple food restaurant in Insadong offering exquisite Buddhist vegetarian cuisine
meals.dinner: Mingles — Michelin-starred restaurant blending Korean traditions with global techniques; reserve the chef's tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Garden tour at Changdeokgung requires advance reservation and is weather-dependent. Balwoo Gongyang requires prior booking. Dress warmly as December temperatures in Seoul can drop below freezing.

day_by_day.morning: Private K-pop and Hallyu culture deep-dive experience. Visit SM Town COEX Artium or HYBE Insight Museum for an immersive behind-the-scenes look at the K-pop industry. Enjoy interactive exhibits, holograms, and exclusive merchandise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Gangnam district — Seoul's most glamorous neighborhood. Visit the iconic COEX Mall and Starfield Library. Stroll along Garosu-gil (Tree-lined Road) for luxury boutiques, concept stores, and chic cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Private rooftop cocktail experience at a sky bar overlooking the glittering Seoul skyline. Followed by a premium Korean BBQ dinner at a top-tier establishment with sommelier-curated Korean natural wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Resort brunch: Avocado toast, smoked salmon, Korean Bibimbap station, and freshly brewed specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Garosu-gil café culture — dine at a premium fusion bistro such as Café Bora or a high-end Gangnam brunch spot
meals.dinner: Palsaik Samgyeopsal or Maple Tree House — premium Korean BBQ with Wagyu-grade pork and beef, private dining room available

day_by_day.notes: HYBE Insight Museum tickets sell out quickly — book online in advance. Gangnam is best explored on foot; the area is very walkable and vibrant in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class with a renowned Korean chef. Learn to prepare signature dishes including Kimchi, Japchae, Galbi (Korean short ribs), and Tteokbokki from scratch using premium seasonal ingredients. Held at a traditional hanok kitchen studio.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Namdaemun Market and Myeongdong for a curated premium shopping and street food experience. A private stylist or guide can assist with luxury Korean skincare and fashion brand discoveries.
day_by_day.evening: Ascend N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower) via private cable car for a breathtaking panoramic view of Seoul's winter skyline. Enjoy a romantic fine dining dinner at the tower's revolving restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light resort breakfast: Congee, seasonal Korean side dishes, premium green teas
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of your morning cooking class as part of the experience
meals.dinner: N Grill at N Seoul Tower — premium French-Korean fusion with 360-degree city views and an extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: Cooking class should be booked at least 3–5 days in advance. N Seoul Tower is especially magical at night in winter with city lights. Dress in layers for the outdoor observation deck.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (approximately 45 minutes from Seoul by private car). Walk the restored fortress walls and explore the traditional Haenggung Palace within the complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Suwon's Paldalmun Gate area and explore the local traditional market. Return to Seoul and check out the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — one of Korea's finest private art museums featuring both classical Korean and contemporary global art.
day_by_day.evening: Immersive K-drama and Korean cinema cultural experience — attend a premium screening or cultural talk, followed by an evening in Itaewon's upscale dining and lounge district.

meals.breakfast: Full Korean resort breakfast with Haemul Sundubu Jjigae (spicy seafood tofu stew) and seasonal banchan
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (Suwon-style grilled short ribs) at a heritage restaurant in Suwon — a dish the city is historically famous for
meals.dinner: Cote Korean Steakhouse or Boccalino at Itaewon — premium steak with Korean marbling techniques or Italian-Korean fusion

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private car for the Suwon day trip for maximum comfort. Leeum Museum may have limited hours — check schedule in advance. Itaewon has a vibrant international dining scene ideal for a relaxed evening.

day_by_day.morning: Premium Korean wellness morning — experience a luxury Jjimjilbang (Korean bathhouse spa) session at a 5-star spa facility. Enjoy jade sauna rooms, salt rooms, charcoal rooms, and premium body scrub (Italy towel exfoliation) with a professional aesthetician.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul. Participate in a private monk-led temple stay experience, including meditation, tea ceremony, and a brief dharma talk.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Cheonggyecheon Stream at night — beautifully lit in winter. Stroll along the illuminated stream and enjoy the peaceful contrast of nature within the urban cityscape. End with a premium tasting menu experience.

meals.breakfast: Light in-spa breakfast: Sikhye (sweet rice punch), seasonal fruits, and light rice porridge
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market — visit this iconic traditional market for premium Bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), Mayak Gimbap, and fresh Yukhoe (Korean beef tartare)
meals.dinner: La Yeon at The Shilla Hotel — Michelin three-starred Korean fine dining, one of Seoul's most prestigious dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: La Yeon reservations must be made weeks in advance — this is one of the hardest tables to secure in Seoul. The temple experience at Jogyesa is a rare and moving cultural highlight. Bring a journal.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the War Memorial of Korea — a deeply moving and educational experience covering Korean history from ancient times through the Korean War and beyond. Includes outdoor exhibits of military equipment and aircraft.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hongdae district — Seoul's creative and youthful cultural hub. Visit independent art galleries, street murals, vinyl record stores, and K-indie music venues. Engage with local artists and designers in pop-up studios.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live K-pop concert or idol fan meeting event if available in December, or enjoy a premium K-pop themed dinner show experience at a dedicated entertainment venue.

meals.breakfast: Resort Western breakfast: Eggs Benedict, smoked salmon bagels, fresh-pressed juices, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Yeonnam-dong neighborhood near Hongdae — dine at a trendy Korean fusion restaurant with modern interpretations of traditional dishes
meals.dinner: Ryunique — innovative fine dining with Korean seasonal ingredients presented with contemporary French technique; tasting menu recommended

day_by_day.notes: Check local concert schedules for December K-pop events — SMTOWN, BigHit, and YG often host year-end concerts. Hongdae is most vibrant in the late afternoon and evening.

day_by_day.morning: Private full-day excursion to the Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) and Joint Security Area (JSA). A licensed and knowledgeable private guide will lead this historically significant tour to the border between North and South Korea — one of the most unique geopolitical experiences in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue DMZ tour — visit Dorasan Station, the Third Infiltration Tunnel, and the Dora Observatory for views into North Korea. Return to Seoul by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing and restorative evening at the resort. Enjoy a private in-suite spa treatment — Korean Hanjeungmak hot stone therapy or aromatherapy massage offered through the resort's luxury spa.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure: Korean Seolleongtang (ox bone soup) and steamed rice for warmth
meals.lunch: Lunch near Imjingak Peace Park — traditional Korean set meal at a local restaurant near the DMZ area
meals.dinner: In-room fine dining experience — resort's premium room service featuring a curated Korean tasting menu with Makgeolli pairing

day_by_day.notes: DMZ/JSA tours require passport and advance booking through an authorized tour operator. Certain areas have photography restrictions. This is a full-day excursion — expect to be out 8–10 hours. Dress warmly.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve morning — private hanbok photoshoot session at a premium studio with professional styling, hair, and makeup. Visit scenic outdoor locations including Gyeonghuigung Palace or Deoksugung Palace for stunning winter holiday photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the festive Christmas atmosphere in Seoul's Myeongdong and City Hall area — beautifully decorated with elaborate light installations for the holiday season. Visit the Seoul Plaza Ice Skating Rink for a festive seasonal activity.
day_by_day.evening: Premium Christmas Eve dinner at one of Seoul's most celebrated fine dining establishments. Seoul transforms beautifully for Christmas with luxury hotel lobbies and restaurants offering special holiday menus.

meals.breakfast: Festive resort Christmas breakfast buffet with special holiday offerings
meals.lunch: Myeongdong Kyoja — legendary hand-made noodle and dumpling restaurant; queue early or book ahead for this beloved institution
meals.dinner: Pierre Gagnaire à Séoul at Lotte Hotel — French haute cuisine by the legendary chef, offering a special Christmas Eve tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Seoul is magical during Christmas. Book the Christmas Eve dinner reservation at least 2–3 weeks in advance. The city's light festivals around Cheonggyecheon and Gwanghwamun are spectacular this time of year.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — leisurely late morning. Enjoy a luxurious Christmas brunch at the resort or a celebrated hotel brunch. Then take a peaceful winter walk through Bukhansan National Park's lower trails — stunning snow-dusted mountain scenery on the edge of Seoul.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Korea — one of Asia's largest and most comprehensive museums. Explore the Korean art and history galleries including the iconic Gyeongcheonsa Pagoda hall. Enjoy the museum's winter garden café.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas gala dinner at the resort or a luxury hotel ballroom event. Celebrate with live music, premium Korean and international cuisine, and festive cocktails overlooking the city.

meals.breakfast: Christmas brunch at the resort — special holiday buffet with roast meats, Korean delicacies, champagne, and festive desserts
meals.lunch: Mountain café near Bukhansan entrance — warm Hotteok (sweet pancakes), roasted chestnuts, and Korean hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Resort Christmas Gala Dinner or Grand Hyatt Seoul's Christmas dinner event — full holiday banquet with live entertainment

day_by_day.notes: Many attractions may have adjusted hours on Christmas Day — verify schedules in advance. Bukhansan trails can be icy in December; wear appropriate footwear. Christmas in Seoul is a national holiday and the city is beautifully festive.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury shopping day — begin at the prestigious Galleria Department Store in Apgujeong, home to Korea's most exclusive luxury brands, designer boutiques, and premium Korean fashion labels. A personal shopping assistant can be arranged.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Apgujeong Rodeo Street and Cheongdam-dong — Seoul's answer to Beverly Hills or Avenue Montaigne. Explore flagship stores of Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Dior alongside cutting-edge Korean designers. Visit a premium Korean beauty concept store for bespoke skincare consultations.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell cultural experience — private Nanta performance (Korea's world-famous non-verbal percussion cooking show) or a traditional Pansori storytelling concert at a premium cultural theater. End with a final celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: Doenjang Jjigae set, soft tofu, steamed egg, and premium Korean tea selection
meals.lunch: Apgujeong dining — Sushi Hyo or a premium Japanese-Korean omakase experience (Seoul has exceptional Japanese dining)
meals.dinner: Gaon — Michelin three-starred Korean fine dining celebrating the full spectrum of Korean culinary heritage; the ultimate farewell dinner

day_by_day.notes: Gaon is arguably Seoul's finest Korean dining experience — reservations must be secured well in advance. Personal shopping services at Galleria can be pre-arranged through concierge. This is a perfect day for premium souvenir and gift shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — gentle sunrise walk or resort spa session. Pack and prepare for departure. Enjoy one last luxurious Korean breakfast at the resort. Visit a nearby café for a final Korean specialty coffee and pastry experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — optional visit to Incheon Airport's cultural zone (traditional craft demonstrations and Korean cultural exhibitions within the airport terminal) or a final stroll through a nearby neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Incheon International Airport. Utilize the airport's premium first-class lounge facilities. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of K-culture, cuisine, and discovery as you depart Seoul.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — full Korean spread: Galbi-tang (short rib soup), steamed rice, assorted banchan, and fresh seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Airport premium dining — Korean Air or Asiana First Class Lounge offers exceptional Korean cuisine, or dine at one of Incheon Airport's acclaimed restaurants
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dinner depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure at Incheon Airport. Incheon is consistently rated the world's best airport — arrive early to enjoy its facilities. Confirm private transfer booking 24 hours in advance. Ensure all duty-free purchases are within customs allowance limits.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX
